Alright. Decided to think on this, as when it comes to moderation, standards are needed, but should always be able to be discussed.

Let's take the complete intro on the term pseudoscience from wikipedia, as while wikipedia itself is not a proper source, it does link to its sources, and is a first step towards a "crowdsourced" definition that frankly has more people, and more critical eyes looking at it (usually). wikipedia.

Pseudoscience is a claim, belief or practice presented as scientific, but which does not adhere to the scientific method.[1][2] A field, practice, or body of knowledge can reasonably be called pseudoscientific when it is presented as consistent with the norms of scientific research, but it demonstrably fails to meet these norms.[3]

Pseudoscience is often characterized by the following: contradictory, exaggerated or unprovable claims; over-reliance on confirmation rather than rigorous attempts at refutation; lack of openness to evaluation by other experts in the field; and absence of systematic practices when rationally developing theories. The term pseudoscience is often considered pejorative,[4] because it suggests something is being inaccurately or even deceptively portrayed as science. Accordingly, those labeled as practicing or advocating pseudoscience often dispute the characterization.[5]

Science is distinguishable from revelation, theology, or spirituality in that it offers insight into the physical world obtained by empirical research and testing.[6] Commonly held beliefs in popular science may not meet the criteria of science.[7] "Pop science" may blur the divide between science and pseudoscience among the general public, and may also involve science fiction.[7] Pseudoscientific beliefs are widespread, even among state school science teachers and newspaper reporters.[8]

The demarcation between science and pseudoscience has philosophical and scientific implications.[9] Differentiating science from pseudoscience has practical implications in the case of health care, expert testimony, environmental policies, and science education.[10] Distinguishing scientific facts and theories from pseudoscientific beliefs such as those found in astrology, alchemy, medical quackery, and occult beliefs combined with scientific concepts, is part of science education and scientific literacy.[11]

This goes beyond my practical first thoughts of "If it is about a new discovery/article/research, must meet the rigors of peer review, the articles/research is not being misrepresented or proven beyond all doubt to be fraudelent, reference explicitly to peer reviewed publications, and if none exist, must be accompanied by a comment explaining its impact, and link to statements about it by people in the field." This is because honestly, and practically, I do not foresee voat as being a primary publication/press point, or being able to gather th resources in academia that the journals have spent their entire existance building. And I know that my first reaction to still allow fake publications prior to discovery, nature link published article, as well as fail to catch straight up fraud at the time of initial publication. However, in these cases, the papers are retracted after the fact, and is at least something. The other thing that I am painfully aware of, is that no matter what the wording is, it should not limit discussion on the next bitcoin paper, that was first disseminated in a mailing list, from an widely speculated source, which has been cited numerous times in ongoing research. Or that whatever the wording ends up, it should be able to cover Mochizuki's abc proof around the time of publication, that we are only now getting a proper retrospective on. This also does not cover educational materials or videos, which I will leave up to others how they feel, I am on the fence, but also understand what I said doesn't cover in this paragraph excludes those submissions, which is why, quoted the wikipedia article first, as it is still properly discusses the term.

The two quotes about the boundary between science, and pseudoscience from this link should not be ignored.

My thinking on the matter is heavily influenced from a recent cases of pop science that I have seen in my newsfeeds. One is the EM drive being tested by NASA. I do not have the skillset to contribute to the debate around it, but the quotes researchers who have pubished in the field, gives it "weight" towards the "science" as opposed to "pseudoscience", which obviously have more to do with the empirical testing being done. The next is kepler alien structure reporting. The original article at the root of the reports which states "By considering the observational constraints on dust clumps orbiting a normal main-sequence star, we conclude that the scenario most consistent with the data is the passage of a family of exocomet fragments, all of which are associated with a single previous breakup event." It is then reported on popular blogs, which do a very good job of balancing "interesting questions or possibilities" with "it is most likely still natural causes". But still shows up recently on the main subverse. When the article itself has "Tabetha Boyajian, Yale University, led the investigations into the mysterious signals and found that the most likely natural cause was the break-up of a comet around the star." buried but it is titled "‘Alien megastructure’ could explain mysterious new Kepler results", which departs from other reporting of "Kepler's 'Bizarre' Signal Sparks Alien Intelligence Speculation" from "Planet Hunters X. KIC 8462852 - Where's the Flux?", we really are seeing the cycle in action (yes, that is completely why I linked press releases, as they do a good job usually of quoting the researchers to "dumb it down for the masses" but also link the papers themselves).

In the end, while entertainment, and not science related, I like how /v/gaming sets up their definitions. It should not be restricted to a word, or a sentence, but a fully explained, logical post, that can be challenged if the wording needs to be updated. Keep the initial wording, so that while you can update the wording, to clarify, it is always the intention from the outset of the intentions towards moderation here. Similarly, this post has gotten away from me. Not even sure how this comes across. Oh, and it should be a general subverses. Wouldn't mind cross posts from the likes of /v/mathematics, /v/physics, /v/biology, wherever. Just a tag in the title, and link to the other subverse's thread in a comment.

Yes, I want to avoid pseudoscience, and the only way to ensure that is having very knowledgeable and dedicated mods that can distinguish between actual science and bullshit. For pseudoscience, there's /v/science, so I'd like this sub to be heavily moderated in order to avoid pseudoscience.
